title: Capacity Estimator — Service Catalog
description: Schema for cloud provider service catalog files (aws.json, gcp.json, azure.json).

region_default.description: Region used for the prices in this catalog (e.g., us-east-1).

last_updated.description: Date this catalog was last verified against vendor pricing.

capacity.description: Per-workload capacity. Keys: rest (RPS), ws (concurrent connections), stream (MB/s).

latency.description: Baseline latency contribution in milliseconds, before queuing penalty.

cost.description: Either fixed monthly cost or a function of load. Use one of: cost_per_hour_usd, cost_per_month_usd, or cost_fn.

cost_fn.description: Cost function — varies by load. Used for serverless/usage-billed services.

rest.description: Cost per unit (request) for REST workload.

ws.description: Cost per unit (connection-hour) for WS workload.

stream.description: Cost per unit (GB) for streaming workload.

notes.description: Free-form caveats (regional pricing, soft limits, etc.).

limits.description: Hard caps that the auto-scale logic cannot bypass — must be remediated (pooler, sharding, ulimit, quota request).

max_connections.description: Connection ceiling. For WS workload, the runtime checks total connections against this and flags a 'hard limit breached' banner when load exceeds it (regardless of how much auto-scale ×N has been applied).

scales_with_instances.description: If true, the limit multiplies with horizontal scale-out (e.g., compute kernel FD — each new instance has its own 65k). If false, it's an absolute ceiling (e.g., DB max_connections — adding more replicas doesn't help; need a connection pooler).

remediation.description: Human-readable advice when the limit is breached, e.g., 'Add PgBouncer / RDS Proxy to pool connections.'
